---
title: "Indicator catalogue"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(gxc)
library(knitr)

# Metadata per indicator and catalogue, taken directly from the installed
# gxc version, so the tables stay in sync with the package
inds    <- unique(gxc_indicators()$indicator)
details <- do.call(rbind, lapply(inds, function(i) {
  d <- as.data.frame(lookup(i)$details)
  d$indicator <- i
  d
}))
```

This page lists all indicators available in `gxc` (version
`r packageVersion("gxc")`) and the catalogues that provide them. The tables
are generated from the package itself. In R, `lookup("<indicator>")` shows
the same information for a single indicator, and `gxc_indicators()` lists
all of them.

## Catalogues in plain words

### What is a catalogue?

A catalogue is one specific dataset that `gxc` can download for you. You
choose it with the `catalogue` argument of `link_daily()` or
`link_monthly()`. The same indicator, for example air temperature, is often
available in several catalogues. They differ in where the data come from,
how detailed they are in space and time, and which region they cover.

### Where do the data come from?

- **ERA5** is a so-called *reanalysis* by the European Centre for
  Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). A weather model is fed with
  millions of past observations (weather stations, satellites, balloons,
  ships) to reconstruct the weather of the whole planet for every hour since
  1940. The result is a complete, consistent picture without gaps, also for
  places without any weather station.
- **ERA5-Land** is a more detailed version of ERA5 for land areas only. It
  covers the period from 1950 and shows finer differences, for example
  between valleys and mountains, but has no values over the sea.
- **DWD** grids are produced by the German Weather Service from its dense
  network of weather stations. They are very detailed but cover Germany
  only.

### How detailed are the data?

- **Spatial resolution** is the size of one grid cell, the smallest area
  with its own value. 0.25° corresponds to roughly 28 km, 0.1° to roughly
  9 km and the DWD grids to 1 km. Every location within one cell gets the
  same value.
- **Temporal resolution** is the time step of the values: one value per day
  (daily catalogues, used with `link_daily()`) or one value per month
  (monthly catalogues, used with `link_monthly()`).

### The catalogues at a glance

- **`derived-era5-land-daily-statistics`** (default of `link_daily()`):
  daily values from ERA5-Land, about 9 km, worldwide on land. Downloaded via
  the Copernicus Climate Data Store, where requests can wait in a queue for
  a long time.
- **`arco-era5-land-daily`** (experimental): the same daily ERA5-Land
  values, but computed by `gxc` from hourly data that are read directly
  from ECMWF's cloud storage. Usually much faster, as there is no queue,
  and it offers more indicators, such as precipitation.
- **`derived-era5-single-levels-daily-statistics`**: daily values from
  ERA5, about 28 km, worldwide including the sea.
- **`reanalysis-era5-land-monthly-means`** (default of `link_monthly()`):
  monthly averages from ERA5-Land, about 9 km, worldwide on land.
- **`reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means`**: monthly averages from
  ERA5, about 28 km, worldwide including the sea.
- **`dwd-hyras-daily`**: daily values for Germany at 1 km from the German
  Weather Service. No registration needed.
- **`dwd-monthly`**: monthly values for Germany at 1 km from the German
  Weather Service. No registration needed.

All ERA5 catalogues require a free account at ECMWF (see
[API access](https://github.com/denabel/gxc#api-access)).

### Overview

```{r catalogues, echo=FALSE}
# Descriptive information per catalogue
info <- data.frame(
  catalogue = c(
    "derived-era5-land-daily-statistics",
    "derived-era5-single-levels-daily-statistics",
    "arco-era5-land-daily",
    "reanalysis-era5-land-monthly-means",
    "reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means",
    "dwd-hyras-daily",
    "dwd-monthly"
  ),
  dataset = c(
    "[ERA5-Land post-processed daily statistics](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/derived-era5-land-daily-statistics)",
    "[ERA5 post-processed daily statistics on single levels](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/derived-era5-single-levels-daily-statistics)",
    "Daily statistics computed by gxc from [ERA5-Land hourly data, ARCO version](https://confluence.ecmwf.int/spaces/CKB/pages/638817583/Analysis+Ready+Cloud+Optimised+ARCO) (experimental)",
    "[ERA5-Land monthly averaged data](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-land-monthly-means)",
    "[ERA5 monthly averaged data on single levels](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means)",
    "[DWD HYRAS daily grids](https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/grids_germany/daily/hyras_de/)",
    "[DWD monthly grids](https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/grids_germany/monthly/)"
  ),
  access = c(
    "CDS API key, request queue",
    "CDS API key, request queue",
    "CDS API key, no queue",
    "CDS API key, request queue",
    "CDS API key, request queue",
    "none",
    "none"
  )
)

cats <- unique(details[, c("catalogue", "temporal", "resolution", "coverage")])
cats <- merge(info, cats, by = "catalogue", sort = FALSE)
cats$n_indicators <- as.vector(table(details$catalogue)[cats$catalogue])
cats$catalogue    <- paste0("`", cats$catalogue, "`")

kable(
  cats[, c("catalogue", "dataset", "temporal", "resolution", "coverage", "n_indicators", "access")],
  col.names = c("Catalogue", "Dataset", "Time", "Resolution", "Coverage", "Indicators", "Access"),
  format = "markdown"
)
```

### Which catalogue should I use?

- **Not sure?** For daily data, start with `"arco-era5-land-daily"`; for
  monthly data, with the default `"reanalysis-era5-land-monthly-means"`.
- **Germany, high resolution:** the DWD catalogues (1 km). No API key needed.
- **Daily data elsewhere, or long baselines:** `"arco-era5-land-daily"`. It
  reads hourly ERA5-Land data directly from ECMWF's cloud-optimised store,
  aggregates them to daily values and is usually
  much faster than the CDS catalogues, whose requests can wait in a queue
  for up to an hour. Its values match `"derived-era5-land-daily-statistics"`.
  It is still experimental.
- **Over sea, or indicators not in ERA5-Land:** the ERA5 single-levels
  catalogues (0.25°).
- **Monthly data:** the ERA5 or DWD monthly catalogues.

## Indicators

Each cell shows the unit of the values returned by that catalogue. An empty
cell means the indicator is not available there.

```{r matrix-fn, include=FALSE}
indicator_matrix <- function(catalogues, labels) {
  d <- details[details$catalogue %in% catalogues, ]
  m <- reshape(
    d[, c("indicator", "catalogue", "unit")],
    idvar = "indicator", timevar = "catalogue", direction = "wide"
  )
  names(m) <- sub("^unit\\.", "", names(m))
  m <- m[, c("indicator", intersect(catalogues, names(m)))]
  m[is.na(m)] <- ""
  m$indicator <- paste0("`", m$indicator, "`")
  m <- m[order(m$indicator), ]
  names(m) <- c("Indicator", labels[match(names(m)[-1], catalogues)])
  rownames(m) <- NULL
  m
}
```

### ERA5 and ERA5-Land

```{r era5, echo=FALSE}
era5_cats <- c(
  "derived-era5-land-daily-statistics",
  "arco-era5-land-daily",
  "derived-era5-single-levels-daily-statistics",
  "reanalysis-era5-land-monthly-means",
  "reanalysis-era5-single-levels-monthly-means"
)
era5_labels <- c(
  "ERA5-Land daily (CDS)",
  "ERA5-Land daily (ARCO)",
  "ERA5 daily",
  "ERA5-Land monthly",
  "ERA5 monthly"
)
kable(indicator_matrix(era5_cats, era5_labels), format = "markdown")
```

### DWD (Germany)

```{r dwd, echo=FALSE}
kable(
  indicator_matrix(c("dwd-hyras-daily", "dwd-monthly"), c("HYRAS daily", "Monthly")),
  format = "markdown"
)
```

## Units and daily statistics

For daily ERA5 and ARCO catalogues, the `statistic` argument of
`link_daily()` sets how the hourly values of a day are combined:
`"daily_mean"` (default), `"daily_maximum"`, `"daily_minimum"` and, for
accumulated indicators, `"daily_sum"`.

Accumulated indicators such as precipitation, snowfall and radiation are
stored as hourly amounts. Their daily mean is therefore an amount per hour
(e.g. `m/h`). Use `statistic = "daily_sum"` for daily totals (`m/day`).
Monthly ERA5 values of these indicators are mean daily totals (`m/day`).
The `.unit` column in the output of `link_daily()` and `link_monthly()`
always states the unit of the returned values.

Temperatures from ERA5 are in Kelvin (K), from DWD in degrees Celsius.

```{r notes, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
notes <- unique(details[!is.na(details$note), c("indicator", "catalogue", "note")])
if (nrow(notes) > 0) {
  cat("### Notes per indicator\n\n")
  for (n in unique(notes$note)) {
    sel <- notes[notes$note == n, ]
    cat("- ", n, " Applies to: ",
        paste0("`", unique(sel$indicator), "`", collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

## Planned datasets

- Hourly resolution, e.g. [ERA5-Land hourly data from 1950 to present](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-land?tab=overview)
  (currently only used internally to compute daily values) and
  [ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/reanalysis-era5-single-levels?tab=overview)
- [Thermal comfort indices derived from ERA5 reanalysis](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/derived-utci-historical?tab=overview)
- [Fire burned area from 2001 to present derived from satellite observations](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/satellite-fire-burned-area?tab=overview)
- [Emission Database for Global Atmospheric Research (EDGAR)](https://edgar.jrc.ec.europa.eu/)
- [CAMS global greenhouse gas reanalysis (EGG4)](https://ads.atmosphere.copernicus.eu/datasets/cams-global-ghg-reanalysis-egg4?tab=overview)
